data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Algorithmic convergence on identical training data and models constitutes a shared cause of failure, making a decentralized network of AI-operated services strictly less resilient than a large service with diverse, human-overseen subsystems.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If small services use locally generated, private training data that is not shared, the convergence mechanism fails.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the large service also uses a single shared training set for all its sub-services, it loses this advantage.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"When small services independently train their operational models on the same public datasets (e.g., the same cloud provider's telemetry), they learn identical failure-detection heuristics. They will all misclassify the same novel anomaly as benign, leading to simultaneous cascading failures. The shared training data is the shared cause. The large service, having 'strictly more total internal redundancy,' can afford to train diverse models on proprietary, artificially noised, or synthetic data, creating an epistemic firewall.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
